subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these six AI-safety events as a stable public core/plugin contract now, and must authorization and exporter support land with the contract?
rationale: The patch freezes a new safety-sensitive public API whose ownership, provenance, privacy guarantees, and plugin authorization semantics cannot be inferred safely from existing diagnostics behavior.

options.title: Land one gated contract
options.body: Sponsor the taxonomy but require runtime validation, trusted provenance, policy-gated plugin emission, core producers, and exporter handling in one reviewable series before exposing the SDK types.

options.title: Keep it internal first
options.body: Develop core-only event producers and sanitized records without public plugin SDK exports until the taxonomy proves stable in real operation.

options.title: Leave taxonomy plugin-owned
options.body: Decline a first-class core taxonomy and let an observability plugin define custom events using existing plugin surfaces.

recommendation.title: Land one gated contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor the taxonomy but require runtime validation, trusted provenance, policy-gated plugin emission, core producers, and exporter handling in one reviewable series before exposing the SDK types.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sets permanent core-versus-plugin ownership and public SDK direction across several companion PRs.
